failures.detail: US-002 ext 3a and US-001 ext 2b are both matchable by the same constructible input with no precedence rule, and prescribe incompatible outcomes. US-002 ext 3a: 'Dataset contains a corrupted record (crash during a previous append, US-001 ext 3c) -> emission moves the corrupted record to the quarantine area, appends the new record ... appends never stay blocked'. US-001 ext 2b: 'Same run_id already present in the dataset -> emission rejected, nothing appended ("duplicate run_id")'. Input: the dataset holds a corrupted record from a crashed append AND a valid record whose run_id matches the incoming record (e.g. an operator re-runs the emission step for an already-recorded run after some other run's crash). Ext 3a says the new record is appended; ext 2b says nothing is appended — both cannot hold. The same overlap leaves a second behavior undefined: when the incoming record is rejected (by US-001 ext 2b or US-002 ext 1a/1b/2a), does the quarantine move of the pre-existing corrupted record still occur? Neither story says. Fix per anchor [Contradiction]: write the boundary condition (e.g. validation/duplicate checks take precedence and quarantine occurs only on a successful append, or quarantine occurs unconditionally before the candidate is judged).
